items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: My old buddy, Eddie Partridge and his wife Mattie, who was a cousin of mine lived in the same house as my father and Eddie and myself had some drinking good times.

ctx.x: We left New York by train the 14th of March. George Duvivier drove us to the New York Central station in his Cadillac and we arrived in Cincinnati the next morning. The air conditioning system had been out of order and the heat was unbearable. We couldn't drink because the drinking water tank was empty and nobody came through selling drinks. We were more than happy to get out of that train.

My father and sister had moved from West 9th street where they were living when we went to Cincinnati in 1954. They were now living in Walnut Hills on Rockdale Avenue. My old buddy, Eddie Partridge and his wife Mattie, who was a cousin of mine lived in the same house as my father and Eddie and myself had some drinking good times.

My brother, his wife, an uncle and cousin John Coleman also lived on the hill and not too far from my father. We gave a party, my brother gave one and many of his or his wife's friends gave parties and that's the way our visit to Cincinnati was spent most of the time. My old boss Clarence Page also invited us to his house as did my good friend from way back, William Smith, who was known as "Smittie" and who had changed his name to Smyth.
